curriculum.lesson_evidence: A balanced plate is a simple guide for a meal: about half the plate vegetables or salad, a quarter grain foods and a quarter protein foods such as lean meat, fish, eggs or legumes, with fruit and a milk food at other times of the day. Portion sizes depend on age, growth and activity. Listening to fullness signals is part of healthy eating, and we talk about foods by their groups rather than calling people or foods 'bad'.
curriculum.scope_limit: Single lesson: partial evidence. Cross-check existing card mapping and NESA content point. Official wording for MA2-RN-01 is recorded in lesson-pipeline/sources/nesa-ma2-rn-01.json where applicable.

Portion sizes depend on age, growth and activity. Listening to fullness signals is part of healthy eating, and we talk about foods by their groups rather than calling people or foods 'bad'.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Describe how Jack could improve a dinner plate that has mostly pasta and a little sauce, using the balanced plate guide.

FEEDBACK
Improvement: halve the pasta, add a large serve of vegetables (in the sauce or as salad) and add a protein food such as lean mince, beans or chicken. The plate then has three groups in better balance.

WATCH FOR
Thinking everyone needs the same portion size. Needs change with age, size, growth and activity, and bodies tell us when they are full.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Draw a balanced dinner plate using real foods your family eats and label each group. Write one change that would make it better balanced and say why, using the words 'half', 'quarter' and 'variety'.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

WORKED MODEL
Example dinner plate: half filled with steamed broccoli and carrot, a quarter with brown rice and a quarter with baked fish. Fruit and yoghurt come later for dessert. Mina eats slowly, listens to her body and stops when she is comfortably full.

TRY FIRST
Describe how Jack could improve a dinner plate that has mostly pasta and a little sauce, using the balanced plate guide.

Improvement: halve the pasta, add a large serve of vegetables (in the sauce or as salad) and add a protein food such as lean mince, beans or chicken. The plate then has three groups in better balance.
teach_steps.explain:
A balanced plate is a simple guide for a meal: about half the plate vegetables or salad, a quarter grain foods and a quarter protein foods such as lean meat, fish, eggs or legumes, with fruit and a milk food at other times of the day. Portion sizes depend on age, growth and activity. Listening to fullness signals is part of healthy eating, and we talk about foods by their groups rather than calling people or foods 'bad'.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the cues, rules or choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For any movement, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby, move at your own comfortable level and stop if anything hurts or feels unsafe. You may always choose a gentler version or only describe the movement. One deliberate, reasoned change is more useful than a longer answer.
